A.explanation: Magnitude about $15\text{ N}$ is too large because the $6\text{ N}$ force has a downward component that partly cancels the $10\text{ N}$ upward force.

B.explanation: Magnitude about $15\text{ N}$ is too large for the same cancellation reason, and $18^{\circ}$ underestimates the sideways pull from the $40^{\circ}$ tilt.

C.explanation: Direction near $37^{\circ}$ is close, but $7.7\text{ N}$ overestimates the resultant because the vertical components subtract rather than add.

D.explanation: Net vertical about $5.4\text{ N}$ up and horizontal about $3.9\text{ N}$ give about $6.6\text{ N}$ at about $36^{\circ}$ to the vertical.

hints: Notice the $6\text{ N}$ arrow points down and to the right, $40^{\circ}$ from the downward vertical dashed line, so its vertical part opposes the $10\text{ N}$ upward force.
Resolve the $6\text{ N}$ force into components parallel and perpendicular to the $10\text{ N}$ force using $6\cos40^{\circ}$ and $6\sin40^{\circ}$.
Subtract to find net vertical force, keep the horizontal component, then combine with $F = \sqrt{F_x^2 + F_y^2}$ and $\tan\theta = F_x/F_y$ for the angle to the vertical.
walkthrough: Resolve the tilted $6\text{ N}$ force. Take upward as positive vertical and rightward as positive horizontal. Its vertical component is downward: $F_{6y} = -6\cos40^{\circ} \approx -4.60\text{ N}$.
Its horizontal component is to the right: $F_{6x} = +6\sin40^{\circ} \approx +3.86\text{ N}$. The $10\text{ N}$ force contributes $+10\text{ N}$ vertical and zero horizontal.
Add components. Net vertical $F_y = 10 - 6\cos40^{\circ} \approx 10 - 4.60 = 5.40\text{ N}$ upward. Net horizontal $F_x \approx 3.86\text{ N}$ to the right.
Find direction to the vertical: $\tan\theta = F_x/F_y \approx 3.86/5.40 \approx 0.714$, so $\theta \approx 36^{\circ}$ to the right of vertical.
A $6.6\text{ N}$ arrow tilted about $36^{\circ}$ from the vertical matches the vector sum. This is option D.
